title: Prescribed split free complex, cell inclusions and canonical cohomology map
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale site $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $C$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on this site. Write $R$ for $C$ with commutativity forgotten, and use the category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For integers $a,b$ and a rank function $r:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf N$, define the split cochain complex $S(C,a,b,r)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] by $S^q=R^{\oplus r(q)}$ if $a\leq q\leq b$, and $S^q=0$ otherwise, with every differential zero. For $a\leq q\leq b$, define $\iota_q:R^{\oplus r(q)}[-q]\to S(C,a,b,r)$ to be the chain map whose degree-$q$ component is the canonical identification with $S^q$ and whose other components are zero. In the derived category with localization $Q$, for every integer $q$, natural number $m$, object $N$ and arrow $f:Q(R^{\oplus m}[-q])\to N$, define its free cohomology map to be the composite $R^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(Q(R^{\oplus m}[-q]))\xrightarrow{H^q(f)}H^q(N)$, using the canonical single-complex homology identification and localization comparison [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. These are explicit constructions; no projectivity, evaluation-exactness hypothesis, splitting theorem, nonempty interval or positive rank is required.
